answer_1.quote: Due to the tediousness of human‑generated counterspeech, the natural language generation (NLG) approach motivates the researchers to focus on generating automated counterspeech...
answer_1.outputs: model‑generated counterspeech texts responding to hateful statements

answer_2.quote: We benchmark CSEval on traditional similarity‑based metrics, as well as multiple popular singledimensional (independent), unified, and LLM‑based evaluators... We report BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, BERTScore, BARTScore, UniEval, PDScore, Pro‑Con, Argument‑Quality, Toxicity Score, and LLM‑based metrics (zero‑shot, G‑EVAL, Auto‑CSEval).

answer_3.quote: LLM‑based evaluators are methods that leverage LLMs to assess the quality of the generated text using natural language instructions or automated prompting techniques... We include zero‑shot baselines of Llama‑3, Mistral, and GPT‑4. Furthermore, we report G‑EVAL, an auto‑CoT prompting framework, and the current state‑of‑the‑art in NLG evaluation. Our proposed Auto‑CSEval method with GPT‑4 as the base model consistently outperforms all the other LLM baselines.

answer_4.quote: We recruited five expert annotators who have either published papers or completed senior theses in the domain of hate speech and counterspeech... annotators are asked to rate the model output across each of the four dimensions on a Likert scale.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate each counterspeech on four dimensions (relevance, aggressiveness, coherence, suitableness) using Likert scales (1‑5 for three dimensions, 1‑3 for suitableness).
